quests.instruction: Choose the reason that best connects to the claim.
quests.prompt: Claim: Employees should be able to start work at different times.
options: People are alert at different times, so choosing hours improves work.
Working hours are written into every employment contract.
Flexible schedules are becoming more common each year.
Employees should be treated with respect at all times.
quests.hint: Ask which sentence explains why flexible starts would be a good idea.
quests.explanation: This reason says how flexible starts improve work. The rest are facts or general statements that don't explain why the change would help.

quests.instruction: Select the TWO reasons that connect directly to the claim.
quests.prompt: Claim: Museums should offer free entry on the first Sunday of every month.
options: First-time visitors might discover an interest in history.
Museums display objects from many different centuries.
Some museums have a café near the main entrance.
Families on small budgets could visit without ticket worries.
quests.hint: Which sentences say what free entry would change for visitors?
quests.explanation: Both correct answers describe results of free entry. The collection and the café exist regardless of ticket prices.

quests.instruction: Choose the best ending for the sentence.
quests.prompt: 'I prefer online banking because ____.'
options: Banks are large buildings in most towns and cities.
Many adults have a bank account of their own.
Banking is an important part of everyday modern life.
I can check my balance at any hour without visiting a branch.
quests.hint: The ending should answer 'Why do you prefer it?'.
quests.explanation: Checking a balance at any hour explains a real advantage. The other endings are true but do not explain a preference for online banking.

quests.instruction: Which claim does this reason support?
quests.prompt: Reason: 'It gives children a place to burn energy after long hours at a desk.'
options: Schools should give students less homework.
Schools should start the day later.
Schools should add a short outdoor break to the morning.
Schools should serve breakfast to all students.
quests.hint: Think about what the reason describes and what it solves.
quests.explanation: Burning off energy after sitting fits an outdoor break. Homework, start time and breakfast are not what the reason is about.

quests.instruction: Which claim does this reason support?
quests.prompt: Reason: 'Customers would spend less time waiting in a line.'
options: Supermarkets should sell more local products.
Supermarkets should install more self-checkout machines.
Supermarkets should stay open later.
Supermarkets should offer a loyalty card.
quests.hint: Which change would reduce waiting?
quests.explanation: More self-checkouts would shorten queues. Longer hours, local products and loyalty cards do not directly reduce waiting time.

quests.instruction: Choose the claim that the reason best supports.
quests.prompt: Reason: 'People who move around more tend to feel less tired in the afternoon.'
options: Workplaces should allow music at desks.
Workplaces should offer free snacks.
Workplaces should end meetings ten minutes early.
Workplaces should encourage short walking breaks.
quests.hint: Connect movement with the claim that would produce it.
quests.explanation: Walking breaks create movement, which the reason links to less tiredness. The other claims may be fine ideas but the reason does not support them.

quests.instruction: Choose the strongest reason to support the claim.
quests.prompt: Claim: Public libraries should offer free internet access.
options: Some libraries already have a few public computers.
Internet access is an interesting kind of technology.
Many people without home internet need it to apply for jobs.
Free things are often popular with local residents.
quests.hint: A strong reason points to a real need or result.
quests.explanation: The right reason shows why free access matters in people's lives. Interest, existing computers and popularity don't show a need.

quests.instruction: Choose the strongest reason.
quests.prompt: Claim: Our football club should train indoors in the winter.
options: Frozen ground raises injury risks and cancels sessions.
Some players enjoy playing football in the snow.
Winter is a cold season in this part of the country.
Indoor halls are used for many different local events.
quests.hint: Which reason describes a problem that indoor training would solve?
quests.explanation: Injury risk and cancellations are real problems. The other statements describe winter or halls without explaining the benefit of moving indoors.

quests.instruction: Select the TWO strongest reasons.
quests.prompt: Claim: Employees should be paid for time spent travelling between client sites.
options: The clients are located in several different cities.
Unpaid travel can make a low-paid role cost more than it earns.
Travel is quite enjoyable for some people.
The travel is part of the job, and the time is not free.
quests.hint: Look for reasons about fairness or cost to the employee.
quests.explanation: The correct reasons argue that the time belongs to the job and can create financial loss. Enjoyment and locations don't argue for pay.

quests.instruction: Choose the reason that addresses the same point as the claim.
quests.prompt: Claim: Reusable bottles are cheaper than buying bottled water.
options: Reusable bottles come in many different colours.
One reusable bottle replaces hundreds of purchases.
Reusable bottles are easy to carry in a school bag.
Reusable bottles look very good on a desk at work.
quests.hint: The claim is about cost. Which reason talks about cost?
quests.explanation: Replacing hundreds of purchases speaks directly about money. The alternatives describe convenience and appearance, which are not the point of the claim.

quests.instruction: Choose the reason that supports the claim about speed.
quests.prompt: Claim: Online shopping is faster than going to a shop.
options: Online shops often have a much larger selection.
An order takes two minutes and needs no travel.
Many online sellers offer big regular discounts.
Delivery drivers often work very long hours.
quests.hint: Stay with the exact quality the claim mentions.
quests.explanation: The best answer is about time saved. Selection and discounts may be advantages, but they don't show that online shopping is faster.

quests.instruction: Choose the reason that fits the claim.
quests.prompt: Claim: Group projects teach students to communicate clearly.
options: Group work can be done in the library.
Teachers can mark one report instead of five.
Students must explain their ideas so teammates can act on them.
Group work saves time compared with individual assignments.
quests.hint: Ask which sentence shows communication being practised.
quests.explanation: Explaining ideas to teammates is communication in action. The other options are about place, time and marking, not communication.

quests.instruction: Choose the sentence that gives a real reason instead of repeating the claim.
quests.prompt: Claim: Buses are a better choice than cars for city centres.
options: Buses are vehicles with several doors.
Many people in city centres own cars.
In city centres, buses are simply the better choice.
Buses carry many people using far less road space.
quests.hint: A reason should add new information rather than say the same thing again.
quests.explanation: The best answer explains why buses are better by pointing to road space. The first alternative repeats the claim, while the others don't explain anything.

quests.instruction: Which sentence gives a real reason?
quests.prompt: Claim: The weekly team meeting should be shorter.
options: A shorter meeting would be better for the team, since everyone would get back to work sooner.
The team would prefer a meeting that does not last so long, and most of them say it drags on.
Most of the important information is covered in the first fifteen minutes.
The meeting is held every Tuesday morning in the large room on the second floor of the building.
quests.hint: Watch out for sentences that say the same thing in different words.
quests.explanation: Only the correct sentence adds an explanation. Two options restate the claim and the last gives a schedule detail.

quests.instruction: Select the TWO sentences that only repeat the claim.
quests.prompt: Claim: Cycling is a healthier way to commute.
options: Riding to work is the healthier choice.
Pedalling gives regular exercise that many office workers lack.
Cyclists avoid sitting still in slow traffic.
Commuting by bike is better for your health.
quests.hint: A repeating sentence uses new words but adds no new information.
quests.explanation: The first two say 'healthier' in other words. The other two explain how cycling improves health.

quests.instruction: Choose the sentence that adds a DIFFERENT second reason.
quests.prompt: Claim: Our town should build a new swimming pool. Reason 1: A pool would let children learn a skill that can save lives.
options: Swimming is a skill that could protect children in water.
It would give adults a low-impact way to stay fit all year.
Children would learn how to swim safely.
A pool would teach young people to swim, which is very useful.
quests.hint: The second reason should introduce a new group or benefit.
quests.explanation: The best answer adds a different benefit for a different group. The other options restate the first reason.

quests.instruction: Which sentence adds a genuinely new reason?
quests.prompt: Claim: Companies should let staff work from home two days a week. Reason 1: Staff save time and money on commuting.
options: Not commuting saves employees a lot of time each week.
Quiet home offices make focused tasks easier to finish.
Staff spend less on fuel and tickets when they stay at home.
Commuting costs can be quite high for many workers.
quests.hint: Reject any sentence that is about the same cost or time as reason 1.
quests.explanation: Concentration is a separate benefit. The other options all return to commuting savings.

quests.instruction: Choose the best second reason.
quests.prompt: Claim: Schools should teach money management. Reason 1: Students will soon need to manage their own money.
options: Financial lessons can show students how maths is used in daily life.
Students leaving school need to know how to spend wisely.
Young people will have to handle their own budgets before long.
Managing money will become a daily responsibility for them.
quests.hint: Look for a benefit that isn't simply 'they will need it later'.
quests.explanation: The maths link is a new reason about learning, not about future need. The rest repeat the first reason.

quests.instruction: Put the sentences in the best order: claim, reason, example, closing.
quests.prompt: Arrange these sentences about family dinners.
options: Last Sunday we put our phones in a basket and talked for an hour.
Conversation is harder when people keep glancing at screens.
A basket by the door is a simple rule worth trying.
Phones should stay off the table during family dinners.
quests.hint: The first sentence states the position. The last one suggests what to do.
quests.explanation: A clear order gives the position, explains why, shows a real example and ends with a practical closing thought.

quests.instruction: Order these sentences from an email to a manager.
quests.prompt: Arrange the sentences of this paragraph from an email about meeting notes.
options: Meeting notes should be sent to the team within a day.
Next-day notes would prevent that kind of confusion.
Last month two of us disagreed about who would send the budget because the notes arrived a week late.
People forget details quickly.
quests.hint: Look for the sentence that opens with the recommendation.
quests.explanation: The email opens with the recommendation, explains why, gives an example of the problem and ends with the benefit.

quests.instruction: Put these sentences from a community post in order.
quests.prompt: Arrange the sentences of this community post about sharing tools.
options: Our neighbourhood should start a tool-sharing library.
Sharing tools would save money and storage space.
Most households use a drill only a few times a year.
Three houses on my street each bought one for the same small job.
quests.hint: Decide which sentence a reader needs first to understand the rest.
quests.explanation: The post starts with the idea, gives the reason, then a concrete example, and finally shows the benefit.

quests.instruction: Choose the example that best fits the reason.
quests.prompt: Reason: Reading regularly improves vocabulary.
options: After a term of novels, my sister used 'reluctant' in essays.
Novels are sold in almost every bookshop in town.
Vocabulary is the set of words that a person knows.
Some students read novels on the bus to school.
quests.hint: An example should show the reason happening in real life.
quests.explanation: The sister's story shows vocabulary growing after reading. The alternatives define, describe or mention reading without showing the effect.

quests.instruction: Choose the best example.
quests.prompt: Reason: Clear signs make public places easier to use.
options: Trains are usually busy in the early mornings.
At the new station, first-timers found their platform alone.
Some stations have very large clocks on the walls.
Many station signs are painted blue and white.
quests.hint: The example must show a result caused by the signs.
quests.explanation: Finding a platform without help shows signs making a place easier. The other statements are unrelated details about stations.

quests.instruction: Which example supports the reason?
quests.prompt: Reason: Cooking at home lets people control what goes into their meals.
options: Many people watch cooking programmes on television.
Restaurants often have large menus with many dishes.
When I make soup myself, I use half the salt restaurants do.
Soup is a popular dish in colder countries.
quests.hint: Look for an example about control over ingredients.
quests.explanation: Using less salt shows control over ingredients. The rest are facts about restaurants, TV and popularity.

quests.instruction: Choose the sentence that best explains how the reason leads to the claim.
quests.prompt: Claim: Schools should start later. Reason: Teenagers need more sleep.
options: Teenagers are students between thirteen and eighteen years old.
With later lessons, teenagers sleep longer and are more alert.
Sleep is important for everyone, whatever their age.
Many teenagers already wake up early in the morning.
quests.hint: Explain what would change if the claim were adopted.
quests.explanation: This sentence connects a later start to more sleep and better attention. The rest state facts that do not link the reason to the claim.

quests.instruction: Which sentence best explains the link?
quests.prompt: Claim: Cafés should give a discount to customers who bring their own cups. Reason: It reduces waste.
options: Each reusable cup replaces a disposable one.
Some cups are made of paper and plastic.
Cafés give discounts on many different things.
Waste is a big problem in many large cities.
quests.hint: The explanation should show how the reason actually happens.
quests.explanation: This sentence shows how a reusable cup means fewer thrown-away cups. The rest give background but no link.

quests.instruction: Which sentence explains the connection?
quests.prompt: A team leader writes: 'We should keep a shared calendar because it prevents double bookings.'
options: Double bookings are inconvenient for the whole team.
Calendars show days, weeks and months in a grid.
A shared calendar is a good idea for every team.
When everyone sees one schedule, nobody books a taken room.
quests.hint: Show how the calendar stops the problem.
quests.explanation: The answer explains the mechanism. The alternatives describe calendars, repeat that double bookings are a problem, or repeat the claim.

quests.instruction: Choose the best way to complete the argument.
quests.prompt: 'I think students should choose their own reading books, because ____'
options: students should choose their own reading books. For example, my cousin finished three novels in a month after picking her own.
teachers have little time to choose books. For example, my cousin finished three novels in a month after picking her own.
they read more when the story interests them. For example, my cousin finished three novels in a month after picking her own.
they read more when the story interests them. For example, our library opens at nine on Saturdays.
quests.hint: Check that the reason explains the claim and the example supports the reason.
quests.explanation: The best answer links reason and example. Others use an unrelated example, a mismatched reason, or repeat the claim.

quests.instruction: Choose the best way to complete the argument.
quests.prompt: 'Managers should ask for feedback, because ____'
options: managers have many tasks to complete. For example, our receptionist spotted a booking error weeks before management did.
staff often notice problems first. For example, the office is closed on public holidays.
staff often notice problems first. For example, our receptionist spotted a booking error weeks before management did.
managers should ask for feedback. For example, our receptionist spotted a booking error weeks before management did.
quests.hint: Each part should lead to the next.
quests.explanation: The reason explains why feedback is useful and the receptionist story proves it. In the others, the example is unrelated, the reason doesn't fit, or the reason repeats the claim.

quests.instruction: Choose the most complete short paragraph.
quests.prompt: A student writes about phone use on buses. Which version contains a claim, a reason and a fitting example?
options: Bus passengers should use headphones for music. Music is enjoyable for many people. Headphones come in many different styles.
Bus passengers should use headphones for music. Playing sound aloud disturbs people who are trying to rest. On my morning bus, two passengers asked a teenager to turn his speaker down.
Playing sound aloud disturbs people who are trying to rest. On my morning bus, two passengers asked a teenager to turn his speaker down. The driver announced the next stop.
Bus passengers should use headphones for music. Playing sound aloud disturbs people who are trying to rest. Buses in our city run every ten minutes.
quests.hint: Check for all three parts, and check that each one connects to the other.
quests.explanation: The first paragraph has a clear claim, a reason and an example showing the reason. The others lack a reason, use an unrelated example, or lack a claim.
